doc.title: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards) Interview, 1948-06-09
doc.interviewee: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards)

title: Opening: introductions at the Jefferson City Buzzards clubhouse, June 1948
summary: Mark Wiley explains the purpose of the recording and members introduce themselves; Simpson is called the last surviving original member.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: We are gathered here at the clubhouse of the Jefferson City Partners Carnival Club. Mr. Simpson, as much as you are the last surviving member of the original group who founded the Jefferson City Partners, we younger members of the club have come to you for some really authentic first-hand information, and we feel certain that you will give it to us for the best of your ability. We are prompted to do this because we believe that the fighters will continue as the granddaddy of the marching clubs around New Orleans for many, many years to come. So what you tell us here this evening, incidentally, which is Wednesday, June 9, 1948, will be of untold historical value to the club or into the future. As signatories to this interview, I think we should all identify ourselves. I am Mark Wiley, and this is...
Thank you. Marley's case, Elliman. And here is Mr. Simpson. You want Mr. Toto? I asked him to correct you so I can answer.
This is Lee Simpson, one of the original members of the club, the only man of the old time and that it arrives today.
And the, uh... It's Brother Mark, another old member. Thank you, Mark. Um, Mr. Simpson, will you give us a short background sketch of yourself? Thank you.
